cities.base: A riad in the northern medina between Mouassine and Ben Youssef, or around Riad Zitoun el-Jdid south of the square.
cities.name: Marrakech

cities.base: Fes el-Bali between Bab Boujloud and Talaa Kebira, on the upper side so you walk downhill to the sights in the morning and take a taxi from Rcif or Bab Guissa back up.
cities.name: Fes

cities.base: Inside the medina within five minutes of Plaza Uta el-Hammam, on the Ras el-Ma side if you want to walk to the Spanish Mosque at dawn. The town is small enough that anywhere in the medina works.
cities.name: Chefchaouen

cities.base: One night in a tented camp inside the erg and one in an auberge in Hassilabied or on the Merzouga dune edge with the dunes behind the pool. Book the camp through the auberge.
cities.name: Merzouga and Erg Chebbi

cities.base: A gîte or small lodge in Imlil itself or in Aremd, the village 20 minutes' walk above it; Aremd is quieter and sits on the Toubkal path so you start the walk from the door.
cities.name: Imlil

cities.base: The medina, anywhere between Place Moulay Hassan and the Skala; it is a grid and you cannot get lost, so pick on price. Rooms facing the sea get the wind and the noise of it all night.
cities.name: Essaouira

cities.base: Not a base. A 300-metre limestone slot 15 km above Tinghir, walked on the Merzouga to Marrakech road; there are hotels in the gorge mouth but the trip does not need them.
cities.name: Todra Gorge

cities.base: Not a base. The hairpin road and the Monkey Fingers rock above Boumalne Dadès, seen on the same road day between Todra and Marrakech.
cities.name: Dadès Gorge

cities.base: Not a base. The mud ksar on the Ounila river, 30 km from Ouarzazate and 3.5 to 4 hours from Marrakech over the Tizi n'Tichka.
cities.name: Aït Ben Haddou

cities.base: Not a base. The trailhead village 30 km from Chefchaouen for God's Bridge and the Akchour cascades; grand taxis from the Chefchaouen bus station, 45 minutes.
cities.name: Akchour and Talassemtane

places.name: Jemaa el-Fna at night
places.note: The square from 19:00 is the reason people come and it is also the hardest three hours of the trip: eat at stalls with locals on the benches, agree a price before the henna or the photo, and walk away from anyone who takes your arm.

places.name: The harira and snail stalls, Bab Agnaou side
places.note: Harira from the 40-year stall on the southwest edge is 5 to 10 dirhams a bowl and the babbouche snail pots on the north side are 15 to 30, the honest end of the square; the numbered grill stalls around 35 pad the bill, so pick a grill by where Moroccans are sitting.

places.name: Mechoui Alley
places.note: A covered lane just north of the square where whole lambs come out of pit ovens from 11:00 at around 260 dirhams a kilo; buy by the quarter kilo from a middle stall, not the famous end one, which has a tourist price, and go before 14:00 because it sells out.

places.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
places.note: The 14th-century Quranic college, reopened in 2022 after restoration, with the finest carved cedar and zellij in the city around a single marble courtyard; 50 dirhams, open 09:00 to 19:00 daily and only until 16:30 in Ramadan, and it is empty at 09:00 and unbearable at 11:00.

places.name: Bahia Palace
places.note: Built in the 19th century for Grand Vizier Bou Ahmed under Moulay al-Hassan I, painted cedar ceilings and orange-tree courtyards; 100 dirhams, 09:00 to 17:00 with last entry 16:30, and the tour groups arrive at 10:00, so be at the gate at opening.

places.name: Saadian Tombs
places.note: Walled up for two centuries and found by aerial survey in 1917, the Chamber of the Twelve Columns is 20 minutes of Carrara marble and cedar seen through a single doorway with a queue; 70 dirhams cash, 09:00 to 17:00, and first thing or last hour is the only time the queue is short.

places.name: Jardin Majorelle and the Yves Saint Laurent Museum
places.note: A cobalt-blue garden of cactus and bamboo, the most photographed thing in Morocco, beside the 2017 Yves Saint Laurent Museum by Studio KO (140 dirhams, 10:00 to 18:30, closed Wednesdays); garden 08:00 to 18:30 daily, tickets online only, and they sell out days ahead in spring.

places.name: The souks from Semmarine to the Kissaria
places.note: Enter by Souk Semmarine and keep north into the dyers', slipper and metalworkers' lanes; anyone who offers to show you the tannery or 'the Berber market, today only' wants 100 dirhams to lose you, so say no and follow the flow of hand-carts, and go before 11:00 when it is still locals shopping.

places.name: Al Fassia, Guéliz
places.note: A women-run Fassi kitchen Marrakech families use for weddings: order the lamb shoulder for two when you book, 300 to 500 dirhams a head with wine, closed Mondays. One listing marked this Guéliz branch temporarily closed in October 2026, so call first; Aguedal is the same kitchen.

places.name: Nomad
places.note: Modern Moroccan on a rooftop above the spice square, cumin-crusted lamb and a good vegetable tagine at 200 to 400 dirhams a head, no alcohol; it is the one medina restaurant worth booking, 2 to 3 days ahead for the 19:00 sunset terrace, and it is tourists only, which is fine once.

places.name: Hammam Mouassine
places.note: A working 16th-century neighbourhood hammam that also takes tourists for a scrub and black-soap gommage at around 150 to 250 dirhams, which is a tenth of a riad spa; bring flip-flops and go in the afternoon slot, and if you want towels and a quiet room go to a riad spa instead.

places.name: Bab Debbagh tanneries
places.note: Smaller and dirtier than Fes with a mandatory 'guide' who materialises at the gate and a leather shop you are steered into afterwards; if you are going to Fes, see the Chouara there and give this one a miss.

places.name: Bab Boujloud and the Talaa Kebira walk
places.note: In through the blue gate, built in 1913 under the French protectorate rather than medieval, and down the main artery to the Quaraouiyine: camel heads at the butchers, the Bou Inania on the right, hand-carts shouting 'balak'; start by 09:00, the faux guides are thickest in the first 200 metres.

places.name: Bou Inania Madrasa
places.note: Built 1350 to 1355 under the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris, the one madrasa in Fes with its own mosque, so non-Muslims see the prayer hall across the courtyard; 20 dirhams, 09:00 to 18:00, it closes longer at Friday prayers, and times shift with prayers, so go first thing.

places.name: Al-Attarine Madrasa
places.note: Smaller than Bou Inania and better: one courtyard of 1325 zellij, carved plaster and cedar with almost nothing restored, beside the Quaraouiyine, whose gates you look through but not pass; 20 dirhams, 09:00 to 17:30 or 18:00 (hours vary, check), and it shuts around Friday midday prayers.

places.name: Chouara Tannery
places.note: The 11th-century vats of pigeon dung and dye seen from the terraces of the leather shops that ring them; the terrace is free with a sprig of mint for the smell, but the shop expects a purchase or a 20-dirham tip, the colours are best in morning light, and the vats are empty on Fridays.

places.name: Nejjarine Fondouk and Museum of Wooden Arts
places.note: An 18th-century caravanserai restored to the last cedar screen, three floors of carpentry and a roof café with the best free view over the medina's centre; around 20 to 30 dirhams but no 2026 tariff was found, so check the price. 10:00 to 17:00, and see the carved fountain outside.

places.name: Jnan Sbil gardens
places.note: The 19th-century royal garden restored in 2011, bamboo, a lake and Fassi families on the benches, free and the only green in the old city; open daylight hours and closed Mondays, and it is the walk between Bab Boujloud and the Mellah.
places.neighborhood: Between Fes el-Bali and Fes el-Jdid

places.name: Marinid Tombs
places.note: Ruined 14th-century Marinid tombs on the hill with the medina below at sunset and the call to prayer coming up in waves. Listed as temporarily closed for restoration, so check it is open; the view is also had from the road, and the Borj Nord arms museum is 500 m west.
places.neighborhood: The hill north of Bab Guissa

places.name: Café Clock
places.note: The camel burger, a decent lunch, cooking classes and Sunday concerts in a restored house behind the water clock; 100 to 150 dirhams a head, a Western crowd, and the roof is the place to recover from the Talaa Kebira at 13:00.
places.neighborhood: Fes el-Bali, Derb el-Magana off Talaa Kebira

places.name: Restaurant Dar Hatim
places.note: A family dining room in their own house, a fixed menu of salads, pastilla and a steamed lamb shoulder or tagine at around 200 dirhams, and the son walks you back to a landmark afterwards; you must book by phone or WhatsApp the day before, there is no walk-in, and it is the best-value dinner in Fes.

places.name: The Ruined Garden
places.note: Lunch among the walls of a collapsed riad, small Fassi plates and a slow-cooked mechoui that needs 24 hours' notice; 150 to 250 dirhams, open 12:00 to 22:00, and the fig-tree courtyard is where a hot afternoon goes.

places.name: The Boujloud grills and Thami's
places.note: From 18:00 the lane inside the gate is brochettes and harira at 8 to 35 dirhams, the snail cart by the gate is 10 for a bowl, and Thami's on the corner does a 40-dirham tagine on plastic chairs that is better than most riad dinners; it is loud and it is where the medina eats.

places.name: Bissara and msemen at Rcif
places.note: Split-pea soup with cumin and olive oil at 6 to 12 dirhams and a msemen pancake off the griddle from 07:00 around the square where the taxis come in; the working breakfast of the medina, no tourist has a reason to be here, and that is why it is good.

places.name: Plaza Uta el-Hammam
places.note: The plane-tree square under the kasbah where everyone ends up at 19:00 with a mint tea; the café terraces are all much the same at 15 to 25 dirhams a tea, the restaurants on it are the worst-value in town, and the cannabis offers start here and are best ignored.

places.name: The Kasbah museum and garden
places.note: The fort Moulay Ali ibn Rashid founded in 1471 against the Portuguese, with a small ethnographic museum, a garden and a tower you climb for the roofscape; 09:00 to 17:30, reviewers report 80 dirhams but no tariff was found so check, and labels are Arabic, French and Spanish only.

places.name: The Spanish Mosque
places.note: The abandoned 1920s Bouzafer mosque, 20 to 25 minutes up from Ras el-Ma, with the whole town below; non-Muslims cannot go in, the hilltop is the point. Sunset fills it with two hundred people, sunrise has ten and the light is better.

places.name: Ras el-Ma
places.note: The spring where the river comes out of the mountain and the women of the town still wash rugs on the concrete slabs; go before 10:00 for the washing, the cafés above it do a 10-dirham tea, and it is the start of the mosque path.

places.name: The blue lanes at 07:00
places.note: The stairs and alleys that are on every phone are the upper medina around Callejon el-Asri and Rue Targhi, and at 07:00 they are empty and being repainted; by 11:00 there is a queue for each staircase and a fee for the pots.
places.neighborhood: Medina, above Rue Sidi el-Haj Aissa

places.name: The Monday and Thursday souk
places.note: Rif farmers bring goat cheese, olives, honey and live chickens to the open ground below Bab el-Ain twice a week; nothing for sale to a tourist except the cheese and it is the most Moroccan hour in a town that has become a photo set.
places.neighborhood: Below the medina, Avenue Hassan II

places.name: Restaurant Beldi Bab Ssour
places.note: A few tables in a lane where the tagines are actually cooked to order, goat cheese salad from the Rif and a 60 to 100 dirham bill; it fills by 20:00 and does not take bookings, so go at 19:00.

places.name: Assaada
places.note: A no-menu cheap place near the lower gate that does kefta brochettes, harira and a chicken-olive tagine at 25 to 70 dirhams for people who live here; plastic tablecloths, the best lunch under 10 dollars in town.

places.name: Restaurant Sofia
places.note: The breakfast plate of msemen, eggs, olives and apricot jam with a nus-nus coffee for 30 to 60 dirhams, and a solid tagine later; a family place, not a scene.

places.name: Café Clock Chefchaouen
places.note: The Fes café's outpost, camel burger, Rif breakfast and a roof terrace with music some evenings; takes cards, which almost nowhere else in town does, and is where to sit out the 15:00 heat.
places.neighborhood: Medina, on the path towards Ras el-Ma

places.name: The Hotel Parador bar
places.note: The only reliable beer in a town without bars, on the terrace of the old Spanish hotel next to the kasbah with the valley below; 40 to 60 dirhams a bottle, and the pool is open to non-guests for a fee in summer.

places.name: Casa Aladdin
places.note: Four floors of painted rooms and a roof with the view, and the tagines are fine, but it is the restaurant every tour group is sent to and the price is 60 to 180 dirhams for what Bab Ssour does for half; go for the terrace tea if you must.

places.name: God's Bridge
places.note: A natural limestone arch 25 metres over the river, 2.4 km up the right-hand trail from the Akchour dam with 200 metres of climb; no entry fee on foot, the path runs at water level and floods in spring, and a tagine kiosk sits at the junction below.

places.name: The Akchour grand cascade
places.note: 5.5 km up the left-hand trail past the small cascade and its swimming pools to a 30-metre fall, 245 metres of climb and a full 4 hours return; strong in April and May and a thread by September, and the last hour is scrambly and slippery.

places.name: The Erg Chebbi big dune at sunrise
places.note: The 150-metre dune behind the auberges, 30 to 40 minutes of two-steps-up-one-back on soft sand to be on the ridge at 06:45 for the sun coming over Algeria; free, best October to April, cold before dawn from November to March, and by 08:00 the sand is too hot to sit on in summer.
places.neighborhood: Erg Chebbi, the dune behind the village auberges

places.name: The camel ride and the tented camp
places.note: An hour and a half on a camel at 16:30 to a camp in the dunes, tagine, Gnawa drumming round a fire and a mattress on the sand or a tent with a real bed; 60 to 120 dollars a head, the saddle hurts after 40 minutes, and the budget camps are 20 tents deep, so pay for a mid-range one.

places.name: Khamlia and the Pigeons du Sable
places.note: A village of Gnawa descendants of enslaved people brought up from the Sahel, where the Pigeons du Sable play iron castanets and gimbri for tea in their house; 50 dirhams and a tip, sessions on demand from about 10:00 to 18:00, and it is the real thing even though it is done for visitors.

places.name: Dayet Srji
places.note: A seasonal salt lake 3 km west of the village that fills after winter rain and gets flamingos and stilts from about February to May, then dries to a white pan; worth a bike or a walk at 07:00 in spring and not worth anything in August.

places.name: Hassilabied village and the palm garden
places.note: The mud-brick village at the north end of the erg where most of the family auberges are, with a khettara-fed palm garden of fig and date plots you can walk through; free, the kids will want a pen, and the dune drops straight into the back gardens.

places.name: Rissani souk
places.note: The Tafilalt's market town three mornings a week, donkeys parked in their own lot, dates by the kilo, sheep, and a spice hall; Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday only, go before 11:00, and the auberge will take you in the 4x4 for 100 to 150 dirhams.

places.name: Medfouna at Rissani
places.note: The stuffed flatbread of the Tafilalt, minced lamb, almonds, onion and spice sealed inside dough and baked in a clay oven, ordered an hour ahead from the ovens by the souk or from your auberge the night before; 50 to 100 dirhams and it feeds two, and it is the one dish here that is not a tagine.

places.name: The 4x4 loop: nomads, Mifis mine and the fossil beds
places.note: A half-day in the auberge's Land Cruiser round the outside of the dunes: the abandoned French-era kohl mine at Mifis, a nomad family's tent for tea, the black fossil plain and Khamlia on the way back; about 250 dirhams a head, and the nomad visit is staged but the family is real.

places.name: Sandboarding on the near dunes
places.note: The auberges lend a board for nothing or 50 dirhams and the dune behind the pool is the run; 17:00 when the sand cools, the walk up is the workout, and it is fun for exactly an hour.

places.name: The dunes after midnight
places.note: Walk 200 metres from the camp fire and lie on the ridge; the nearest town of any size is 50 km away, the Milky Way is overhead from May to September, and a new moon week is the thing to check when you book.

places.name: Quad bikes in the erg
places.note: Two hours at around 300 dirhams with a guide and helmet, and every camp within earshot hears you; the dunes are the quiet and the quads are the thing that removes it, so if you want speed do it at Merzouga village and not near the camps.

places.name: The Todra narrows walk
places.note: Walk the road and the riverbed through the 10-metre-wide section between 300-metre walls, 1 to 2 km each way, 20 minutes in the shade before 09:30 and a coach park with carpet sellers by 11:00; free, and the climbers on the walls are the show.

places.name: The Tinghir palm grove
places.note: The irrigated palm grove below Tinghir with its kasbahs and channels, seen from the roadside belvedere above or walked from the old town; an hour and free, and the Todra alternative when the gorge itself is a car park.

places.name: The Tissadrine hairpins
places.note: The road that folds up the canyon wall in six switchbacks, photographed from the terrace of the café at the top; free, it is an open roadside viewpoint, 45 minutes each way from Boumalne, and the gorge runs on another 10 km if you have time, which on the Marrakech day you do not.

places.name: The Monkey Fingers at Tamellalt
places.note: Eroded red conglomerate pillars along the river, free to see from an open roadside lay-by; best in the low light of 16:30 to 18:00, which is the wrong time for the Marrakech drive, so give it 20 minutes, or walk through them for 90 if you split the drive here.

places.name: The Aït Ben Haddou ksar
places.note: The mud ksar from Gladiator and Game of Thrones, crossed by footbridge and climbed to the granary on top in 45 minutes; a 10 to 20 dirham entry at one of the family houses, five families still live inside, and 08:00 or 17:00 is the difference between a village and a film set full of coaches.
places.neighborhood: Aït Ben Haddou, across the Ounila

places.name: Sidi Chamharouch
places.note: The mule track from Imlil through Aremd to the white boulder shrine at 2,350 m, 600 metres up, tea at the stalls and back in 4 to 5 hours; no guide needed this far, the shrine is not for non-Muslims to enter, and Fridays bring pilgrims and mules in both directions.

places.name: Aremd village
places.note: The largest village in the valley, a stack of stone and mud houses on a rock above the walnut terraces, 20 minutes' climb from Imlil; free, the gîtes here are quieter than Imlil's, and the view up the Mizane to Toubkal is the reason to sleep here.

places.name: The Toubkal refuge, 3,200 m
places.note: Refuge du Toubkal and Les Mouflons side by side at the valley head, 5 to 6 hours and 1,450 metres up from Imlil, dormitory beds and a hot dinner for about 250 to 350 dirhams half board; a licensed guide is compulsory past the Aremd checkpoint, and it is cold and airless at night.

places.name: Toubkal summit, 4,167 m
places.note: A 05:00 start from the refuge, 3 to 4 hours of scree to the iron pyramid on top with the Sahara haze one way and the Atlantic the other, then 5 hours down to Imlil; guide about 500 dirhams a day, crampons and axe from November to April, and altitude headaches are normal above 3,500.

places.name: Tizi n'Tamatert
places.note: The 2,279 m pass on the piste to Tacheddirt, 2 hours up from Imlil and the best free view of the Toubkal massif without a guide; the road is drivable and taxis use it, so you can walk up and ride down.

places.name: Tacheddirt
places.note: A terraced village at 2,300 m on the far side of the pass where a gîte does a 60-dirham lunch and nobody sells rugs; 3 hours' walk from Imlil or a 150-dirham taxi over the pass, and the valley beyond is empty.

places.name: Lunch at the Kasbah du Toubkal
places.note: The converted caid's fort on its rock above Imlil serves a Berber lunch on the terrace to non-guests at EUR 40 a head on its 2026-27 price list (EUR 25 lunch plus a EUR 15 non-resident supplement); book a day or two ahead, and it is the one splurge worth making in the valley.
places.neighborhood: Above Imlil, 15 minutes on foot or by mule

places.name: Chez les Berbères
places.note: A village restaurant doing the tagine and the omelette-with-everything for 60 to 90 dirhams on a terrace over the stream, 4.7 on 258 Google reviews, 07:00 to 23:00 daily; the alternative to the gîte's dinner, which is usually the same tagine cooked better.

places.name: Asni Saturday souk
places.note: The valley's market at the junction town on the Marrakech road, mules, sheep, spices and second-hand shoes in a walled ground on Saturday mornings only; on the way up or down, and 45 minutes is plenty.

places.name: The Imlil waterfall and the Achain orchards
places.note: A 30-minute climb through the walnut and apple terraces to a small fall with a tea stall, the walk the gîte will send you on the afternoon you arrive; free, easy, and a trickle by September.

places.name: Tizi n'Mzik and the Azzaden valley
places.note: The 2,489 m pass west of Imlil, 2.5 hours up, then down into the Azzaden valley to Tizi Oussem and out by taxi, or back the same way; 900 metres of climb, almost nobody on it, and a guide is sensible because the descent path is not obvious.

places.name: The port fish grills
places.note: Choose the fish from the ice at one of the numbered stalls, it is weighed and grilled with bread, salad and a soft drink; the city posts prices per kilo so agree the weight and the total before it hits the grill, sardines and sole are the honest choice, and the lobster is the tourist trap.
places.neighborhood: Between the port and Place Moulay Hassan

places.name: The fishing port at 08:00
places.note: The blue boats come in, the gulls fight over the gutting, and the auction is on the quay; free, smells of fish and diesel, and the best hour to see what the grills will be selling at noon.

places.name: Skala de la Ville
places.note: The 18th-century sea rampart with its bronze cannons and Orson Welles's Othello behind it, free and the sunset spot, with the woodworkers' cellars underneath selling thuya boxes; go at 18:00, the wind on top is real, and it can shut after sunset in some seasons, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Skala du Port
places.note: The other bastion, with the tower you climb for the classic view of the boats, the ramparts and the island; 60 dirhams for foreigners in a 2025 guide, 09:00 to 17:00, and one listing says free and closed Monday, so hours vary, check and verify at the gate. 45 to 90 minutes.

places.name: Bayt Dakira
places.note: The House of Memory, a museum since 2020 built around the 1882 Simon Attias synagogue in the Mellah, on a town whose Jewish half was a third of the population until 1960; free, and one listing says 09:00 to 19:30 daily against 10:00 to 18:00 closed Saturdays, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Triskala
places.note: A stone-vaulted room doing a daily fish plate for 60 to 80 dirhams, vegetable dishes that are not an afterthought, and anise bread; cash, no alcohol, and the best value dinner in the medina.
places.neighborhood: Medina, Rue Touahen behind the Skala

places.name: The Loft
places.note: Grilled octopus and a prawn pasta in a room of 1960s chairs, 120 to 200 dirhams a head, no licence; the sort of place a local architect eats, and it needs a booking on weekends.

places.name: MIMTI
places.note: Modern Moroccan from a small farm-led kitchen, salt-cured sardines on flatbread, a seafood couscous on Fridays and a sardine kefta tagine on Saturdays; 100 to 180 dirhams, and the one lunch here that is not a tagine or a fish plate.

places.name: The Salut Maroc rooftop
places.note: A tiled hotel roof over the ramparts for a beer or a glass of Val d'Argan wine at sunset, 50 to 90 dirhams; Essaouira has no bar culture, so this and the Taros-era rooftops on the square are the choice, and the wind decides which.

places.name: The beach walk to Diabat
places.note: Two hours return along the hard sand past the kite school to the Borj el-Berod ruin sinking into the sea and the path up to Diabat, the village that trades on a Jimi Hendrix visit that lasted a week; free, and from 15:00 the wind is in your face on the way back.

places.name: Sidi Kaouki and Chez Momo
places.note: A long empty surf beach with a marabout on the point, bus 2 from Bab Doukkala for 10 dirhams or a grand taxi, and Chez Momo at the beach end grilling the day's sole and sardines for 30 to 80 dirhams; the day with nothing to buy, and the water is 18C.

places.name: Coopérative Marjana argan
places.note: A women's cooperative on the Marrakech road where the nuts are still cracked by hand between two stones and the oil is what it says on the label; free to watch, fair fixed prices, and the bus from Marrakech passes it so ask the taxi to stop.

places.name: Dar El Bacha, Musée des Confluences
places.note: Built in 1910 for Thami El Glaoui, pasha of Marrakech, and a museum since 2017: the cedar door painted in poppy, indigo and saffron, the painted ceilings and zellij columns; 60 dirhams, 10:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays, and Bacha Coffee is inside.

places.name: El Badi Palace
places.note: The Saadian sultan Ahmad al-Mansur's palace, built 1578 to 1593, now a ruin round a 90 by 20 metre pool with storks on the walls and a gallery in the tunnels; 70 dirhams, doors close 17:00 so arrive before 15:00, and walk the wall top for the view.

places.name: Koutoubia Mosque and gardens
places.note: Founded in 1147 by the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min and rebuilt about 1158, its 77-metre minaret is the model for Seville's Giralda; non-Muslims cannot go in, so it is free from the garden and the ruins of the first mosque, best at 08:00 or the sunset call.

places.name: Maison de la Photographie
places.note: Photographs of Morocco from 1879 to the 1960s on glass plates and postcards, founded in 2009 by Hamid Mergani and Patrick Manac'h, with a roof café over the medina; 80 dirhams, which also covers the Mouassine music museum, 09:30 to 19:00.

places.name: Le Jardin Secret
places.note: A 19th-century palace complex with an Islamic garden and an exotic one, and a tower over the Mouassine roofs for 40 dirhams more; 100 dirhams, daily from 09:30, closing 17:30 in November and December and later the rest of the year, last entry 30 minutes before.

places.name: Mouassine Mosque and fountain
places.note: Built 1562 to 1573 for the Saadian sultan Moulay Abdallah al-Ghalib, with the fountain beside it part of the same complex; free from the street, since non-Muslims cannot enter, and it sits on the walk from the souks to Le Jardin Secret.

places.name: Snack Toubkal
places.note: The budget set-menu tagine place on the edge of the square, 4.2 on 3,956 Google reviews, 07:00 to 23:30 daily; set menus of 65 and 75 dirhams a head in undated Wanderlog reviews, so read the board before you sit.

places.name: Dar Batha Museum
places.note: A late 19th-century palace begun by Sultan Hassan I, a museum since 1915 and reopened in February 2025: the ceramics go back to the early 14th century, and the Andalusian garden is the rest stop; 60 dirhams, 10:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays, no DSLRs.

places.name: Ibn Danan Synagogue
places.note: A 17th-century synagogue in the Mellah, finished around 1701 and restored with the World Monuments Fund in the 1990s, when a mikveh turned up in 1997; no visiting hours or price were found, so ask your riad and check the price, and pair it with the Jewish cemetery.

places.name: Café Fatima, Hassilabied
places.note: The village café Tripadvisor ranks top in Hassilabied, 4.7 on 311 Google reviews: a Berber omelette breakfast for about 4.50 euros or a grilled plate with fruit for about 10 euros a head (July 2025 review); 08:00 to 22:30, Saturdays to 22:00.

places.name: Restaurant Nora, Khamlia
places.note: Lunch in Khamlia, 4.6 on 1,159 Google reviews, so pair it with the Gnawa music there: a 9-euro fixed menu of starter, main, fruit and water (July 2024) or a 90-dirham Berber pizza (December 2023); it shuts at 19:00, so not for dinner.
places.neighborhood: Khamlia, Route de Taouz, 7 km south

places.name: Restaurant La Baraka, Rissani
places.note: The lunch stop on a Rissani souk morning (Tuesday, Thursday, Sunday), 4.7 on 427 Google reviews, 10:00 to 22:00; about 14 dollars a head on an undated tour-lunch page, and reviewers call it a bit pricey for Morocco, so check the price.

places.name: Kasbah Tamadot, Asni
places.note: Richard Branson's hotel above Asni takes outside bookings through OpenTable, lunch 12:00 to 16:00 and dinner 19:00 to 23:00. Its 2026 lunch menu has a chicken tagine at 280 dirhams, about $29 for one main, so a full meal runs well above that.

places.name: Mosque and University of al-Qarawiyyin, exterior
places.note: Founded in 857 by Fatima al-Fihri, once Morocco's largest mosque and counted the West's first university. It is a working mosque, so plan on a look through the gate doors from the lane, free, then Place Seffarine 100 m away.

places.name: Mausoleum of Moulay Idriss II, exterior
places.note: The shrine of Idris II, who founded the town in 808 as his capital, under green-tiled roofs; entry is for Muslims only, so you see the carved doorway and the wooden bar across it from the lane. Free, hours vary, check.

places.name: Place Seffarine, the coppersmiths' square
places.note: The small square of the coppersmiths, beside the dyers' and tanners' souk and al-Qarawiyyin; they mostly repair old metalware now but still hammer it by hand, so come in the working morning. Free.

places.name: Bab el-Makhzen, the Royal Palace gates
places.note: The golden doors of the 13th-century royal palace, which is closed to visitors and heavily guarded, so this is a photo from the square; free, and the Mellah with the Ibn Danan synagogue and the Jewish cemetery is next door.

places.name: Borj Nord Museum (arms museum)
places.note: A fortress built in 1582 under Sultan Ahmed el-Mansour, now 5,000 weapons and a roof over the medina. Listed free (undated), so check the price; 09:00 to 17:00 with a lunch break, longer on Friday, closed Monday, 500 m west of the Marinid Tombs.
places.neighborhood: Fes el-Bali, the hill above Bab Boujloud

places.name: Dar al-Magana, the water-clock house
places.note: The Marinid-era water-clock facade facing Bou Inania, free from the street; sources disagree on its date and on whether the clock is still there, since it was removed for research, so treat it as a 10-minute look on the way to the madrasa.

places.name: Grand Mosque of Chefchaouen, exterior
places.note: The 15th-century mosque with the octagonal minaret on the square under the kasbah; it is a place of worship, so look from Uta el-Hammam, free, and pair it with the kasbah tower view.

places.name: Place El Haouta
places.note: A small square with a fountain locals still fill water at and cafés round it, 130 m west of Uta el-Hammam with a fraction of its tour groups; free, and the better place for the afternoon tea.

places.name: Bab Souk, the market gate
places.note: The old gate where the local market sits outside the medina, best on Monday or Thursday; few reviews and listings disagree on where the souk ground is, so ask your riad where it sets up that week.

places.name: Slat Lkahal Synagogue
places.note: Restored from 2010 with UNESCO help, with two hekhals and a Tuscan-style retable said to be unique in North Africa; free with a donation box, 10:00 to 17:00, shut from Friday 15:00 to Sunday 10:00, and if locked a number on the door reaches the caretaker.

places.name: Haim Pinto Synagogue
places.note: Once the home of Rabbi Chaim Pinto, with a blue-tiled prayer room upstairs above offices; free, 09:00 to 18:00, closed Saturday, and 80 m from Slat Lkahal, so do the two together.

places.name: Musée Sidi Mohammed Ben Abdellah
places.note: The town museum of sepia photographs, weapons, jewellery and guembri lutes, small and with only 12 Google reviews. Listed as temporarily closed, so check it has reopened, check the price, and hours vary, check.

places.name: Mausoleum of Moulay Ali Cherif, Rissani
places.note: The tomb of the forebear of the Alaouite dynasty that still rules Morocco; the tomb room is for Muslims, so you get the courtyard and garden, free, 08:00 to 18:00. Shut Sunday, so pair it with the Tuesday or Thursday Rissani souk.
places.neighborhood: Rissani, the south edge of town

places.name: Hassilabied gardens
places.note: Berber family plots watered by khettara underground channels, with a view over the dunes and almond blossom in mid-February; free, and only a handful of reviews, so ask at your auberge before walking in.

outings.why: 460 km on the N13 over the Middle Atlas: the Azrou cedars and their macaques at 90 minutes, Midelt for lunch at 3.5 hours, the Ziz gorge tunnel and the palm-grove belvedere at 5, then Erfoud and the erg appearing at 8.
outings.name: The Fes to Merzouga road, with Azrou and the Ziz
outings.season: All year; the Tizi n'Talghomt pass at 1,900 m can close.
outings.fallback: The Supratours night bus from Fes, 10 hours, 200 dirhams, no scenery.

outings.why: From the hotels at the gorge mouth walk the narrow section along the river for 1 to 2 km, 300-metre walls either side, then back; an hour on foot, but it is 3 hours' drive from Merzouga so from there it fills the morning.
outings.name: The Todra gorge walk
outings.season: All year; flash floods can shut the road for hours.
outings.fallback: The Tinghir palm grove walk from the town, 90 minutes, no drive.

outings.why: Drive up the Dadès valley to the Tissadrine hairpins and the Monkey Fingers (90 minutes return from Boumalne), then Skoura, Ouarzazate, Aït Ben Haddou and the Tizi n'Tichka at 2,260 m into Marrakech.
outings.name: The Dadès hairpins and the road to Marrakech
outings.season: All year; the Tichka closes for snow a few days each winter.
outings.fallback: Split it: sleep in Aït Ben Haddou or Ouarzazate and do the Tichka the next morning.

outings.why: Cross the river, climb through the ksar to the granary on top for the view over the Ounila, 45 minutes up and down; the 3 hours is from Ouarzazate with the drive, and from Marrakech it is a 10-hour day of which 8 is the car.
outings.name: Aït Ben Haddou
outings.season: All year; 40C at midday June to August, go 08:00 or 17:00.
outings.fallback: Telouet kasbah on the old Tichka road, half the crowds, 45 minutes off the N9.

outings.why: The first third of the Toubkal path: Imlil to Aremd across the walnut terraces, then up the Mizane valley on the mule track to the white-painted boulder shrine at 2,350 m, tea at the stalls, and back; 600 m of ascent, no guide required.
outings.name: Sidi Chamharouch
outings.season: All year; snow above Aremd from December to March.
outings.fallback: Imlil to Aremd and back through the orchards, 90 minutes.

outings.why: Up the piste east of Imlil to the 2,279 m pass for the view back to Toubkal, then down to the terraced village of Tacheddirt for lunch and a taxi back, or walk both ways.
outings.name: Tizi n'Tamatert and Tacheddirt
outings.fallback: Imlil to Tamatert village and back, 2 hours.

outings.why: Grand taxi 45 minutes to Akchour, then the right-hand trail up the Farda to the natural rock arch (5 km return, 200 m) and the left-hand trail to the grand cascade (11 km return, 245 m); doing both is 5 hours on foot.
outings.name: God's Bridge and the Akchour cascades
outings.season: March to November; the cascades are fullest in April.
outings.fallback: God's Bridge only, 2 hours on foot.

outings.why: Out through Bab el-Ansar past Ras el-Ma and 20 minutes up the path to the empty 1920s mosque on the hill for the whole blue town in first light; sunset is the famous slot and has two hundred people on it, sunrise has ten.
outings.name: The Spanish Mosque at dawn
outings.fallback: Ras el-Ma and the cafés above the washing pools, 40 minutes.

outings.why: Bus 2 or a grand taxi 25 km south to a long empty surf beach with a marabout on the point, a fish lunch at Chez Momo and a walk as far as you like; it is the day with nothing to buy.
outings.name: Sidi Kaouki
outings.season: All year; the water is 18C at best.
outings.fallback: The Essaouira beach walk to the Borj el-Berod ruin at Diabat, 2 hours return.

outings.why: From 19:00 the square turns into 100 food stalls, storytellers, Gnawa musicians and snake men; eat harira and snails standing up, brochettes at a stall where locals are sitting, and keep your hands off the monkeys and the henna women.
outings.name: Jemaa el-Fna after dark
outings.season: All year; in Ramadan it starts after the sunset cannon.
outings.fallback: Watch it from the Café Glacier or Kabana terrace with a juice, then go home.

outings.why: Taxi to Borj Nord or walk up from Bab Guissa, 20 minutes, to the ruined tombs on the hill above the medina for the whole of Fes el-Bali going gold at 18:00 while the call to prayer comes up from 300 mosques; nothing to pay.
outings.name: The Marinid Tombs at sunset
outings.fallback: The Borj Nord terrace, same view, 20 dirhams.

destination.name: Morocco
destination.pitch: Twelve days is exactly enough to do the medinas of Marrakech and Fes, the blue town, the dunes at Merzouga and a night in the High Atlas without living in a car, but only if you accept two long road days and skip Casablanca entirely.
destination.caveat: The distances are the trip: Fes to Merzouga is a nine-hour day and Merzouga to Marrakech is ten with the gorges, the Marrakech medina hustle wears people down by day three, and during Ramadan (roughly 8 February to 9 March 2027) most restaurants and street food shut until sunset. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Marrakech has real nightlife in Guéliz and the square at 21:00 is the best free show in Africa, but neither Fes nor Essaouira is a late city.
because.food: Tagines cooked for the family table at Al Fassia and Dar Hatim, harira and snails on Jemaa el-Fna, camel at Café Clock, and sardines grilled by weight on the Essaouira quay.
because.nature: Erg Chebbi is 150-metre dunes you sleep in, Todra is a 300-metre limestone slot you walk through, and Toubkal is the highest peak in North Africa two hours from Marrakech.
because.culture: Two of the world's oldest continuously working medinas, a 9th-century university, Saadian tombs, Marinid madrasas and Gnawa music that came up from the Sahel and still plays in Khamlia.
because.adventure: A two-day Toubkal ascent from Imlil, the Akchour canyon to God's Bridge, camels into the erg and the hairpins of the Dadès all fit inside one trip.
because.relaxation: Essaouira is the only base where nobody is selling anything, and a riad courtyard with a hammam is the point of the afternoon in Marrakech.
because.exploration: The Fes medina is 9,000 car-free lanes with no map that works, and every souk, fondouk and tannery in it is still doing the job it was built for.
